summary: Through the Desert is a Knizia abstract where players snake colored camel trains across a hex desert, trying to reach oases and enclose territory while blocking rivals from doing the same. It plays fast and is easy to teach, but has real bite because routes can be sealed off with a single well-placed piece.
praised: elegant, easy-to-teach rules hiding real depth
tense spatial blocking reminiscent of Go
criticised: can feel visually and thematically dry
hidden scoring until the end can surprise new players
less satisfying at low player counts

interaction.kind: direct spatial blocking of opponents' caravan routes and contested oases
interaction.detail: Camels are placed on a shared hex desert where an opponent's tribe can physically wall off your route to an oasis or a bonus region, so much of the game is choosing placements specifically to cut off rivals rather than just grow your own network. Because the desert is one shared grid with no private board, essentially all meaningful decisions are made in reference to what others are doing.
interaction.said: frequently compared to Go, with players noting caravans "block" each other and fight over the same oases

scoring.how_you_win: You place camels to build the longest caravans of each color, reach oases, and enclose water holes; scores are hidden until a player runs out of camels, then the highest total wins.
